discovery: Quantum simulation of strongly correlated Hubbard models with ultracold atoms in optical lattices

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and LMU Munich, Germany

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum many-body physics
motivation: Zoller and co-workers showed theoretically (1998) that ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise the Bose-Hubbard model, with interactions and tunnelling tunable at will. Bloch and Greiner made this real by observing the quantum phase transition from a superfluid to a Mott insulator (2002), the first controlled realisation of a strongly correlated textbook model with neutral atoms. Greiner's quantum gas microscope and Bloch's single-site imaging and control then made it possible to see and manipulate individual atoms in correlated many-body states, revealing antiferromagnetic order, string patterns and magnetic polarons in the Fermi-Hubbard model, and many-body localisation. Together this work founded analogue quantum simulation. It now links atomic physics with condensed-matter theory and underpins today's neutral-atom quantum processors. It is a new way of doing many-body physics: we build the Hamiltonian and then measure it atom by atom.
